itemListElement.name: Granola vs Fathom in 2026: Which Fits US Teams Better?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Granola vs Fathom debate, Granola is better for private, bot-free notes that start from what you type. For recording calls, sharing clips and syncing to a CRM, Fathom wins. Neither is better for every team, so run both on 3 real meetings before deciding.

Yes. The free plan includes unlimited recordings and transcriptions plus instant AI summaries. Some AI features carry a "limited use" tag, and Premium costs $16 a month billed yearly. Since it works with Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, the free plan is useful for most US teams from day one.

Partly. The free Basic plan includes AI notes and chat, but it keeps only 30 days of meeting history. Business costs $14 per user per month and removes the history limit. Students and accepted startups can get 12 months of Business free, and registered nonprofits get 50% off, through Granola's help center programs.

mainEntity.name: Does Granola record video like Fathom?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Granola transcribes your computer's audio and writes notes, but it does not record video. Clipping and sharing moments is a Fathom feature. If you need to replay a moment, such as a customer's exact wording, that makes Fathom the better fit; people who only need the notes are fine with Granola.

mainEntity.name: Which works better for Google Meet and Zoom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zoom and Google Meet work with both. Fathom joins as a recorder, while Granola captures audio from your desktop app on Mac or Windows, and only Fathom also supports Microsoft Teams. Granola needs its app open during the call, whereas Fathom joins automatically from your calendar, which makes it easier to standardize across a team.

mainEntity.name: What is a good alternative to both Granola and Fathom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lynkk combines bot and bot-free capture, in-person recording, and follow-up work like Jira tickets. It is free for 5 notes a month and $15 a month on Pro.
